transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to turn my brain off. I'm constantly worrying about, well, basically everything all at once. I worry about my marriage, if I'm messing things up at work, paying the bills... even just the house projects I start and never finish. It's like this constant loop in my head that I'm just failing at everything, especially as a husband and a dad. It's just gotten to be too much.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or don’t get pleasure from things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I still care about all those things. I still want to spend time with my wife and kids, and I still like my hobbies. It's not that I've lost interest or don't want to do them... it's just hard to actually relax and enjoy them right now because my mind is always racing with everything else I'm worried about. But the interest itself is definitely still there.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel depressed or hopeless. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself because I can't seem to shut my brain off, but I'm not feeling sad or down most of the time. It's really just the constant stress and the overthinking, not depression.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, or trouble sleeping, that come along with all this worrying?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound tight almost all day. It's like my shoulders are just locked up and I'm constantly bracing for something. And the restlessness is definitely there... I catch myself pacing a lot, like between my meetings at work, or just tapping the pieces when I'm at chess club. It just feels impossible to actually sit still right now.
